6.resolved: ö = o + U+0308 (COMBINING DIAERESIS), NFD. All other characters ASCII.
6.note: The three plate numerals are printed as typographic small capitals — 'V', 'VII', 'XIV' — flattened here to ASCII capitals. This is English-register typography, not notation: keying_spec.md §2.3 licenses small-cap base codepoints only for the notation series, 'The key glosses ᴀ ᴇ ɪ jointly as "obscure vowels (short)"; ʟ merely shares the shape family', and there is no small-cap V or X sort in the inventory at all. Note in particular that the I of 'XIV' is ASCII I and NOT U+026A: §5.7's medial-small-cap class is scoped to Tier-1 forms, and this is an English roman numeral. Plate V is the reading. (An earlier version of this note claimed the first numeral measured the same height as the V of 'VII'. It does not: at 4x the v sits at plain x-height while VII and XIV are small caps, visibly taller. Corrected per keying_spec.md 5.12. The reading is unaffected — keying_spec.md 2.12 makes every roman numeral plain ASCII whatever its setting, so no height comparison was ever needed) — consistent with data/loi.json's plates I–XXXV, and with 'Fig. 2' being a plate-internal figure number rather than text-figure 2. Döring is a German proper name, Tier-2, keyed as printed with its diaeresis. NOTE FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: 'harness proposal check' flags this token under the keying_spec.md 5.1 rare-form arm ('sets a character the corpus sets in only 4.9% of 122 - check for a dropped mark'), so the page does not check silent. The flag is a false positive by construction and the text is deliberately left as it stands: that prior is computed over Tier-1 marked-vs-bare distributions, and this is a Tier-2 German surname where the diaeresis is orthographic rather than notational. The mark is not an absence-shaped call of the kind 5.1 warns about - both dots are plainly set and separated above the o at 2x in review/1-022/zoom/zoom2-002.png, so there is nothing here that a dropped-mark reading could be hiding.

contamination.note: NOT blind, and stated plainly. `harness ocr gaps` and `harness ocr lines --store mz` were run in one batch before the raster was opened, so the CATMuS text of all 8 lines was visible before the first look at scans/chukchi-1-022.png. Every line was nevertheless read off the raster and the sheets, and the reading departs from the machine text in three places: the folio '2' (which mz has nowhere, being outside the polygon), 'Plates V' (mz reads lowercase 'v'), and the English semicolon spacing. The exposure is low-consequence here because the page carries no Tier-1 material at all — CATMuS's 0%-of-inventory blindness and its ASCII substitutions (' ’ / for ˊ, i I r for ɪ) have nothing to bite on — but the sequencing was mine and is recorded rather than glossed.
contamination.tier1: None. This page is entirely English prose plus one German proper name (Döring). No Chukchee, Koryak or Yupik form appears on it, so keying_spec.md §5.1-5.3 (dropped g̣, ɪ/i/r, ä/a) and §5.5/§5.8 (stress vs apostrophe) have no instance to apply to. No U+02CA, no U+0323, no small-cap notation sort is keyed anywhere on the page.
